plan.summary:
Health checks now give up after two seconds. `probe` sends an HTTP GET with a 2-second timeout and returns the status code. `run_checks` also runs a new cache check.

- `probe()` in `service/probe.py` uses `httpx.get(url, timeout=2.0)` and adds `status` to its JSON result.
- `run_checks()` in `service/health.py` adds `check_cache()` to the list.
plan.riskRationale: The change is small. It adds a timeout to one probe and one more check. A timeout error from httpx is not handled in the shown code, so failure behavior needs a check.
plan.storyArc: The probe now makes a real HTTP call with a bounded wait. The health runner then gets a third check. The two changes are separate.

topics.title: Probe makes a timed HTTP request
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `probe` now behave, and what happens when the URL is slow? Verify that no code catches `httpx` timeout errors, and check the callers of `probe`.

topics.title: Health runner adds cache check
topics.narrativeBrief: Which checks does `run_checks` now run? Verify that `check_cache` exists in `service.checks`. The list order is db, queue, cache.
